translationRepairs: Xiao Aludai, whose courtesy name was Yixin, came from the Wuwei tribe.
Xiao Aludai, whose courtesy name was Yixinyin, came from the Wuwei tribe.
字乙辛隱 is a three-character courtesy name; idiomatic Yixin drops 隱, and Yixinyin restores the full romanization without changing the rest of the sentence.
Xiao Aludai, courtesy name Yixin, was a man of the Wuwei tribe.
Xiao Aludai, courtesy name Yixinyin, was a man of the Wuwei tribe.
Literal likewise truncates 乙辛隱 to Yixin; Yixinyin matches the Chinese courtesy name while preserving the rest of the wording.
In the third year of Qiantong, for keeping Song captives who should have been sent back as slaves, he was dismissed from office.
In the third year of Qiantong, for keeping as slaves Song captives who should have been sent back, he was dismissed from office.
坐留宋俘當遣還者為奴 means he kept as slaves Song captives who ought to have been repatriated; “sent back as slaves” misattaches 為奴 to the repatriation clause, and the proposed reordering fixes that relation.
During Shoulong he rose through several posts to tiyin and vice director, and was granted the title of meritous minister who preserves integrity.
During Shoulong he rose through several posts to tiyin and vice director, and was granted the title of meritorious minister who preserves integrity.
保節功臣 is rendered meritorious minister who preserves integrity; idiomatic meritous is a misspelling of meritorious and does not change the Chinese honorific.
During Shoulong he was repeatedly promoted to Tiyin, concurrently Vice Director, and granted the title Meritous Minister who Preserves Integrity.
During Shoulong he was repeatedly promoted to Tiyin, concurrently Vice Director, and granted the title Meritorious Minister who Preserves Integrity.
Literal Meritous is the same misspelling of Meritorious for 保節功臣; correcting the spelling restores the standard English rendering of 功臣.
